A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MT-GRPO. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen2.5-3B post-training experiments on three-task and nine-task mixtures, including sampling and regularization ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original 7B-model evaluations, component ablations, sequential-training comparisons, and runtime analyses.

M1.justification: The stated robustness objective in Equation (5) changes from subtracting epsilon Omega(z) to adding it, with Omega also rescaled. This is a limited objective correction: the implemented GRPO loss, improvement-aware update, and Algorithms 1–2 retain their procedures.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates Countdown, Zebra, and string-based ARC across difficulty levels. v2 retains this coverage and adds MATH and SciKnowEval scientific QA, covering biology, chemistry, physics, and materials science, including a heterogeneous mathematics/ARC/science mixture.

E2.justification: The original GRPO, SEC-GRPO, DAPO, and SEC-DAPO comparisons remain. v2 substantially expands comparison methods with sequential GRPO and DAPO under two task orderings (Figure 14), plus explicit IWU-only and uniform-weight RPS-only controls (Figures 10–11).

E3.justification: The original experiment settings are retained. New protocols include 150-step Qwen2.5-7B and OLMo-3-7B-Instruct training, selection of each OLMo method's best-worst-task checkpoint, sequential training for 240 steps per family under two orderings, and evaluation at a fixed 80-hour budget.

E4.justification: v1 already examines task-weight dynamics, RPS/AAS removal, and reward-only regularization. v2 adds component-isolation ablations across both original settings, detailed gradient-mixture diagnostics, sequential-order and forgetting analyses, and computational-overhead versus wall-clock convergence analysis. The retained RPS ablation also gains an ARC accuracy comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the empirical comparisons. New runtime averages and training curves do not introduce repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original headline and regularization results are retained, while v2 adds substantial results. In the new Qwen2.5-7B experiment, MT-GRPO at lambda=0.2 reports 37.6% worst-task and 51.8% average accuracy versus DAPO's 25.0% and 58.3% (Figure 8). New OLMo results reach 45.8% worst-task accuracy (Figure 9), and the 80-hour comparison reports 53.6% versus DAPO's 43.2% (Table 1). These are newly reported comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix B.1 is substantively corrected in v2 Appendix C.1: the Lagrangian signs and task-weight coefficients change, and the induced regularizer loses its factor K. v2 explicitly acknowledges that eliminating multipliers only establishes sum(z)=1; restricting z to the simplex produces a surrogate. This replaces v1's claimed equivalent reformulation and repairs central mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The two central methodological contributions and the abstract's headline gains remain unchanged. Introduction contribution (iv) broadens the claimed empirical scope from planning and ARC to 3B/7B models, scientific QA, and mathematics, accompanied by an explicit larger-model generalization claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning IWU/RPS complementarity, order-dependent forgetting in sequential training, and how faster convergence offsets sampling overhead. Its new limitations paragraph explicitly restricts demonstrated robustness to the training-task mixture and identifies dependence on verifiable rewards, qualifications absent from v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds measured computational costs and documents model variants, training budgets, and lambda values for the new evaluations. The original optimizer, hardware, rollout, and sampler details remain; the existing code link merely moves to Appendix E. Full dataset and training specifications for the 7B experiments remain incomplete.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the expanded evaluation, including MATH, OLMo 3, and the Qwen2.5 technical report. The substantive positioning against distributionally robust optimization, multitask optimization, and GRPO research is largely retained in the relocated related-work section.

P1.justification: Most existing exposition remains intact with local wording edits. Related Work moves from Section 7 to Appendix A, supplementary experiments receive dedicated subsections, and limitations and impact statements are added. Citation style, author presentation, and acknowledgments also change, while the core narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 reformats the main text and references into two columns and substantially changes display placement and sizing. It adds evaluation, ablation, forgetting, and runtime figures plus Table 1. The old Figure 8 becomes an expanded Figure 16 with an ARC accuracy panel; the original regularization figures are retained as Figures 20–21.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the paper by correcting the central Lagrangian argument and its equivalence claim, testing beyond the original model and synthetic task families, and adding component and sequential-training controls. The wall-clock analysis directly addresses whether extra sampling cost undermines the efficiency claim, while explicit limitations better bound applicability. Missing uncertainty estimates and incomplete 7B reproducibility details remain weaknesses, but the mathematical corrections and targeted empirical evidence provide a clear substantial net improvement.
